BUG (ordering): deep-review-auto.yaml:208 instructs the setup step to pass the RAW review_focus and :231 interpolates it as --review-focus="{review_focus}" inside a shell command, while the sanitiser that strips C0/C1 controls, U+2028/U+2029 and enforces the 1000-char bound runs inside the child process (fanout-run.cjs:161, :168). Sanitisation after the shell cannot protect the shell, so a focus containing a double quote, backtick, $(...) or newline breaks or injects into the composed argv before normalizeReviewFocus is reached - the same threat the function docstring names, one layer earlier.

OVER-ENGINEERING / drift seam: one review-focus normalization contract is implemented three times - stated in deep-review-presentation.txt:69, applied again by step_normalize_review_focus at deep-review-auto.yaml:486, and implemented in fanout-run.cjs:161. The runner copy must stay because it alone protects the review_focus: binding and the native argv; the removable duplicate is the presentation-layer copy, and no test asserts the copies agree.

OPERATOR UX: the review-focus failures name the internal camelCase field, not the flag the operator typed - 'reviewFocus must be at most 1000 characters, got N' (fanout-run.cjs:168) and 'reviewFocus must be a text value' (fanout-run.cjs:161). This is a second instance of the field-name defect class already recorded for the if_cli_* branch placeholders in this lineage, now on a sibling surface.
